name: TLP184(GB-TPL,SE
title: TLP184(SE: AC-input phototransistor photocoupler, 80 V, 3750 Vrms, SO6
summary: A single-channel photocoupler whose input is a pair of GaAs infrared emitters wired back to back, so it responds to input current of either polarity, driving an NPN phototransistor with collector and emitter brought out. The collector-emitter rating is 80 V and the current transfer ratio at ±5 mA is 50 % to 600 %, sorted into the ranks Y, GR, GB and BL; GB covers 100 % to 600 %. It comes in a four-lead SO6 surface-mount body with 5.0 mm creepage and clearance, isolated to 3750 Vrms for one minute, and runs from -55 °C to 110 °C.

circuits.title: Collector current ratio test circuit
circuits.description: Measures how evenly the two input emitters drive the phototransistor. Current is forced into pin 1 (IF1) and then, reversed, into pin 3 (IF2), with the collector held at VCE = 5 V and the emitter grounded; the collector currents IC1 and IC2 for the two directions are compared.

parts.note: collector bias; IC1 or IC2 is measured at this terminal

circuits.title: Switching time test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit for the ton, ts and toff figures at VCC = 5 V, IF = 16 mA and RL = 1.9 kΩ. A current pulse enters pin 1 and returns from pin 3 through a resistor to ground. The phototransistor is a common-emitter switch: emitter to ground, collector pulled up to VCC through RL, and the output VCE taken at the collector.

parts.note: input return resistor; no value given

notes: ton runs from the rising edge of IF until VCE has fallen to 0.5 V; ts runs from the falling edge of IF until VCE has risen back to 0.5 V; toff runs from the falling edge of IF until VCE reaches 4.5 V.

operation.text: Intended for programmable logic controllers and private branch exchanges.
Two GaAs infrared emitters are connected in inverse parallel between pins 1 and 3, so the input takes current of either polarity, AC or DC.
An NPN phototransistor with only its collector (pin 6) and emitter (pin 4) brought out; there is no base lead. Its collector-emitter breakdown is 80 V min and its emitter-collector breakdown 7 V min.

Parts are graded by current transfer ratio at ±5 mA and 5 V: Y 50 % to 150 %, GR 100 % to 300 %, GB 100 % to 600 %, BL 200 % to 600 %, and unranked 50 % to 600 %. With the input at ±1 mA and VCE at 0.4 V, the GB rank still gives at least 30 %.
The collector current with -5 mA input is 0.33 to 3 times, typically 1 times, the collector current with +5 mA input.

Input current is limited to ±50 mA rms up to 90 °C and falls by 1.5 mA per °C above it, reaching 20 mA at 110 °C. Collector dissipation is 150 mW up to 25 °C, falling by 1.5 mW per °C; input dissipation (100 mW) falls by 2.0 mW per °C above 25 °C. Total dissipation is 200 mW. Pulsed input may reach ±1 A for pulses of 100 µs or less at 100 Hz.

Creepage and clearance are each 5.0 mm min and the internal insulation is 0.4 mm thick min. Isolation is rated with the input pins joined and the output pins joined: 3750 Vrms for 60 s at up to 60 % relative humidity, isolation resistance 10¹⁴ Ω typ at 500 V, and 0.8 pF between the two sides.

UL1577 (file E67349); cUL under CSA Component Acceptance Service No.5A (file E67349); VDE to EN60747-5-5 with option (V4); CQC to GB4943.1 and GB8898 for parts from the Thailand factory, with the CQC approval limited to use at altitudes up to 2000 m.

With 16 mA input, VCC = 5 V and RL = 1.9 kΩ, ton is 0.5 µs, ts 30 µs and toff 50 µs typ. With VCC = 10 V, IC = 2 mA and RL = 100 Ω, tr is 2 µs and tf, ton and toff 3 µs typ. Typically toff and ts lengthen as RL rises, toff to about 1.5 ms at 100 kΩ, while ton stays below 1 µs; all three lengthen as temperature rises.
The characteristic curves are typical values, not production-tested limits, unless a curve states otherwise.
The reflow profile is set by package surface temperature and may be run once or twice; all mounting passes should be finished within two weeks of the first.
Preheat to 150 °C package surface temperature for 60 s to 120 s, then 260 °C for no more than 10 s; one pass only.
With an iron, keep the lead at 260 °C or less for up to 10 s, or at 350 °C or less for up to 3 s, and heat each lead once only.

Keep stock at 5 °C to 35 °C and 45 % to 75 % relative humidity, away from moisture, direct sun, corrosive gases and dust, and where temperature changes little, since condensation corrodes the leads. Use anti-static containers once parts leave their packing, put no load on them, and check solderability of parts stored more than two years.
SO6 outline (Toshiba 11-4M1S) with leads only at positions 1, 3, 4 and 6; weight 0.08 g typ.
